reviews.one_line_contribution: A bank-swap diagnostic (D_swap = acc(own bank) - acc(swapped bank)) that quantifies how much of a reflectively-optimized instruction's gain is bound to the particular experience bank it was optimized against, plus a cost-annotated head-to-head of five candidate fixes in which the load-bearing new contrast is optimization-time memory masking (p=0.5) versus the zero-cost deployment-time alternative of lowering injection top-k on an already co-adapted instruction (E2/P8).
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two threats, neither engaged adequately. (1) The RAG robustness-to-context-perturbation literature the proposal itself concedes (FiD-style stochastic document dropping; Yoran et al.-style training with irrelevant/randomized retrieved context) already establishes the general result that randomizing retrieved context during optimization buys robustness to changed retrieved context at deployment. The proposal moves this from weights to instruction text, which is a venue change, not a mechanism change, and makes P2 a low-surprise prediction. (2) More damaging for the *diagnostic*: overfitting of automatically-optimized prompts to the exact trainset/demonstration set they were searched against is well-documented in the MIPROv2/DSPy and APE/OPRO line (validation overfitting, demonstration-order and demonstration-identity sensitivity). The proposal's argument that MIPROv2 'freezes the demo set so there is no turnover' defends against priority on the *setting*, not on the *finding*: a reviewer will say P1 restates known prompt-search overfitting with a memory bank playing the role of the demo set. Separately, the research brief handed to the authors explicitly names ReasoningBank and '2026 successors' as the relevant memory line, and the Related Work never mentions ReasoningBank at all - an omission of prior work the authors were literally given.
reviews.strongest_objection: The study's own power analysis defeats its own pre-registered decision rules. Measurement states plainly that it 'can adjudicate effects of roughly 3 points and larger under the swapped bank and cannot resolve smaller ones' - yet the rules that decide what the paper concludes all turn on smaller quantities: baseline-1/P8 declare memory dropout unnecessary if reduced-k comes 'within 1.5 points' of it; baseline-2 declares 'just optimize memory-free' if p=1 ties p=0.5 within 2 points; P2 requires p=0.5 to beat p=1 by >=2 points. Three of these are equivalence claims, and none is backed by an equivalence procedure (TOST) powered at the stated margin - failing to reject a 1.5-point difference at MDE~3 is guaranteed, not informative. The realistic outcome is therefore that E2 returns a top-k effect that is neither clearly smaller nor clearly equal to the dropout effect, and P8 - the arm the authors themselves call the most likely way the method dies and one of only two confirmatory tests - cannot be decided in either direction. Compounding this, D_swap as designed is not identified as co-adaptation: instructions are optimized only on split A, so acc(B_A) - acc(B_B) confounds instruction-to-bank co-adaptation with a plain bank main effect (B_B may simply be the weaker distillation). The single hand-written instruction evaluated across three banks is a one-observation, zero-variance handle on that main effect and cannot carry the identification of the paper's primary diagnostic. And because B_A and B_B are distilled from disjoint i.i.d. splits of the same HotpotQA distribution, the swap is an exchangeable resample rather than the incremental self-editing turnover the motivation describes; the most likely Stage-1 outcome is D_swap < 3 points, the gate fires, and the paper is a bounded null on one task with one 7B model.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Counterbalance the swap: optimize at p=0 on split B as well and evaluate crossed (A-instructions on B_A/B_B and B-instructions on B_B/B_A), reporting the instruction x bank interaction rather than a one-directional difference. The re-optimization baseline already produces 3 B-optimized instructions; evaluating them on B_A costs 2,400 episodes and converts D_swap from a confounded difference into an identified interaction. Fund it by dropping E4, whose n=21 pooled Spearman is confounded by condition (p=0 instructions have high verbatim overlap and high D_swap by construction, so rho>=0.5 is a design artifact, not evidence of mechanism). (2) Re-specify every 'within X points' rule as a TOST with an equivalence margin the design is actually powered for, and raise the margins to >=3 points or raise n/seeds until 1.5 points is resolvable; as written the paper cannot conclude what its own contingency table says it will conclude. (3) Add a same-size random/shuffled-content bank at deployment, so 'swapped' is separated from 'any bank other than the one I saw'. (4) Actually run the dated preprint search now, including ReasoningBank and 'prompt optimization validation overfitting / distribution shift', and report it - the promise to search 'before submission' is not reviewable.
reviews.missing_baseline: The counterbalanced (bidirectional) swap: instructions optimized on bank B_B evaluated on B_A. The plan optimizes on split A only and evaluates on {B_A, B_B, none}, so the primary diagnostic D_swap cannot be separated from a bank-quality main effect except via a single deterministic hand-written instruction. Secondary omission: a random-content / shuffled bank of matched size at deployment, which would distinguish 'the instruction is bound to *this* bank' from 'the instruction degrades under *any* unfamiliar bank' - the neutral-block arm tests optimization-time perturbation, not deployment-time bank identity, and does not cover this.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is not thin - it is empty, and the authors say so: 'Every web-search call in this session returned a hard server-side tool use limit exceeded error; not one query returned data', with 'zero verified evidence' and novelty 'unverified'. Under the standard that an unsearched novelty claim is a weakness rather than a neutral, this is the single largest deduction, and it is the second consecutive draft in which the search failed. The honesty is creditable and the comparative restructuring is a sensible hedge, but a reviewer cannot grade a search that will happen 'before submission'. I cannot name a specific colliding arXiv preprint under the no-search constraint of this review either, so I score novelty on what is established rather than on what might exist - and what is established is that the intervention is conceded as non-novel (FiD-style document dropping, randomized retrieved-context masking) and the framing rests on an unchecked belief. The planned query list is also incomplete in ways the authors could fix from the materials in hand: it omits 'ReasoningBank' (named in the track brief they were given), 'prompt optimizer overfitting validation set', 'DSPy distribution shift robustness', and 'in-context demonstration dropout', which are the searches most likely to surface a collision with P1.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A bank-swap protocol that quantifies how much of a reflectively-optimized instruction's gain is bound to the particular experience bank present during optimization, plus a pre-registered head-to-head of five candidate fixes (optimization-time memory masking, shard randomization, deployment-time top-k reduction, bank curation, full re-optimization) with the honest possibility that a deployment-side knob wins and the proposed method is unnecessary.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two threats. (1) MIPROv2 (Opsahl-Ong et al., EMNLP 2024): the proposal dismisses it because the bootstrapped demo set is 'frozen', but MIPROv2's Bayesian search evaluates instruction candidates against *different sampled demonstration sets* across trials and minibatches, which is already exposure to a varying in-context distribution — i.e. the paper's own prescription ('randomize the optimization-time context') is arguably already instantiated in the standard optimizer, and the MIPROv2 demonstration-slot arm is precisely the arm dropped for budget. A reviewer will read that as cutting the comparator that most threatens the contribution. (2) The RAG irrelevant-context-robustness line — RetRobust (Yoran et al., ICLR 2024), Chain-of-Note, RAAT, and FiD-style stochastic document dropping — already establishes that training/prompting under randomized or corrupted retrieved context buys robustness to a changed retrieval distribution. The proposal cites only the FiD-style prior and only as a 'mechanistic prior'. Neither line runs a bank-swap on an *optimized instruction*, so the diagnostic itself survives; but 'instruction evolved against fixed context is brittle to context turnover, and randomizing context during search fixes it' is a corollary a reviewer will regard as already known in substance, which is why the novelty score is low even though the specific measurement is not published.
reviews.strongest_objection: D_swap is not identified. D_swap = acc(own bank B_A) − acc(swapped bank B_B) confounds co-adaptation of the instruction to bank content with a plain quality/coverage asymmetry between B_A and B_B, which are built from two different training splits and never counterbalanced (every optimization run in E1 is on split A; only the re-optimization baseline touches B_B, and it never evaluates instr_B on B_A). The design's own logic exposes this: at p=1 the instruction has never seen any bank, so D_swap at p=1 is *by construction* a pure bank-quality difference — yet P1 asserts 'D_swap ≤ 1.5 points at p=1' as a prediction, which is really an untested assumption of bank symmetry smuggled in as a falsifiable claim. Worse, the Stage-1 gate ('proceed only if D_swap at p=0 ≥ 3 points') can be passed by B_B simply being the weaker bank, licensing 33,600 episodes chasing an artifact; and if B_B is the *stronger* bank, real co-adaptation is masked and the study stops at a false bounded null. The hand-written × 3 banks cells contain the correction, but the estimand is never defined as a difference-in-differences, so the headline number and the gate are both stated on the confounded quantity. Compounding this: the setting most likely to make the effect real (ALFWorld / interactive agents, where an ExpeL-style trajectory bank is load-bearing) was cut, and HotpotQA with a 7B model — where distilled 'insights' plausibly move accuracy by well under the 3-point resolution limit — was kept precisely because it is the one that fits the power budget. The most probable outcome of the 21 runs is a bounded null in the setting least likely to exhibit the phenomenon.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Redefine the primary diagnostic as a difference-in-differences: [acc(instr_p, B_A) − acc(instr_p, B_B)] − [acc(hand-written, B_A) − acc(hand-written, B_B)], and restate the Stage-1 gate and P1/P7 thresholds on that quantity, not on raw D_swap. (2) Counterbalance the swap: add >=3 seeds of p=0 optimized on split B and evaluated on B_A, so bank asymmetry is estimated rather than assumed; this is affordable inside the stated envelope by trading the E5 deference-clause arm (6,400 episodes), which is exploratory. (3) Add a same-distribution turnover control B_A' (a resampled/regrown shard of split A) so 'the bank changed' is separated from 'the bank came from different data' — without it, the paper measures split shift, not turnover, and Limitation 8 concedes the abrupt swap is already the maximal case. (4) Select deployment k on a validation split; as written, P8 picks the 'best k in {1,2}' on the same 800 confirmatory items used for the pre-registered test, which contaminates one of the two Bonferroni-protected confirmatory contrasts. (5) Drop or downgrade the 'effect exceeds twice the measured between-seed SD' rule — with 4 seeds the SD estimate has ~3 df and its own CI spans roughly half to double the truth, so this criterion has undefined operating characteristics in a paper whose selling point is measurement rigour; report the mixed-effects interaction CI and the seed-sign agreement instead. (6) Verify the between-seed SD of 1-2 points in the actual pipeline during Stage 1 rather than importing it from a pilot on a different (three-stage cascade) setup; the entire power argument rests on it. (7) Execute and log the dated preprint search before, not after, committing the framing.
reviews.missing_baseline: The counterbalanced swap (p=0 instructions optimized on split B, evaluated on B_A) together with a same-distribution bank-refresh control (B_A', a resampled shard of split A). Without these, D_swap cannot be attributed to co-adaptation rather than to B_A/B_B quality asymmetry or to split shift. Secondarily missing: (a) MIPROv2 with its own demonstration resampling as the existing-practice comparator — dropped for budget, yet it is the strongest 'this is already standard' rebuttal; and (b) an irrelevant/random-bank injection cell at each p level, which would show whether D_swap tracks content match at all or is just a function of injected token volume — the pilot's own volume-is-the-lever finding predicts the latter, and E2 only tests volume on the p=0 arm.
reviews.preprint_collision: Inadequate, and the proposal says so itself: the check reports that every search call failed and that it has 'zero verified evidence', for the second revision running. By the standard that an unsearched novelty claim is a weakness rather than a neutral, this is a substantial negative, and it is the main reason novelty is scored 4 rather than 6 — a proposal whose central contribution is 'nobody has run this diagnostic' has not attempted to establish that. The listed pre-submission query set is a promise, not evidence, and it arrives too late to inform the design (e.g. if a preprint already reports retrieval-context randomization during prompt search, the E1 grid is the wrong grid, not just a scooped grid). I am likewise restricted from searching here, so I can name only candidate collisions from background knowledge, all unverified: the 2025-2026 agent-memory wave (ReasoningBank, A-MEM, Mem0, Memento and similar) which evaluates learned memory transferred across task distributions and would trivially yield a bank-swap number; DSPy/GEPA robustness and prompt-transfer reports; and the RAG noise-robustness line (RetRobust, Chain-of-Note, RAAT) for the mechanism. The one genuine mitigation is structural and I credit it: restating the contribution as a cost-annotated comparison of five fixes means a preprint that merely names the co-adaptation problem does not scoop the paper. That limits the blast radius; it does not substitute for the search.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A bank-swap protocol that quantifies, in item-paired accuracy points against a measured null-replicate floor, how much of a reflective prompt optimizer's gain is bound to the particular experience bank present during optimization, plus a pre-registered head-to-head of five candidate fixes whose load-bearing question (P8) is whether that fragility is curable at deployment by lowering injection top-k or requires randomizing the optimization-time memory context.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two threats, neither adequately dispatched. (1) Mechanism and framing: the proposal itself concedes FiD-style stochastic document dropping and randomized retrieved-context masking in RAG training curricula as the mechanistic prior, and MIPROv2/GEPA already select a final candidate against a fixed validation context, so 'the optimizer overfits the context it was tuned on' is the standard validation-overfitting story from the DSPy/MIPROv2 line rather than a new phenomenon; the only new element is that the context is a self-edited bank instead of a bootstrapped demo set, and the proposal never argues why that distinction changes the mechanism. (2) The demonstration-sensitivity literature (Min et al., 'Rethinking the Role of Demonstrations', and its successors) already establishes that quantity/format of in-context exemplars, not their content, drives most of the effect. That is exactly the pilot's 'injection volume, not content, was the causal lever' finding, and it is precisely what the neutral-block arm (P6) and the top-k arm (P8) are set up to re-derive. If either lands, the paper collapses into a known generic result about context volume, and the proposal's own pre-registration says it would then retitle. ExpeL/AWM/SSO are correctly characterized as non-threatening, since none evaluates an optimized instruction under bank turnover; they are not the danger.
reviews.strongest_objection: The primary diagnostic is degenerate and the one non-degenerate contrast is underpowered at its true unit of analysis. D_swap = acc(own) - acc(swapped) is minimized to zero by any instruction that simply ignores the memory block, so P1's 'D_swap <= 1.5 at p=1' is a manipulation check, not a prediction: memory-free optimization cannot co-adapt by construction. The only claim that distinguishes 'robustness' from 'learned to ignore memory' is P2's 'p=0.5 beats p=1 by >= 2 points under B_swap' — and that contrast is 4 optimizer seeds vs 4 optimizer seeds. Item-pairing over 800 questions does nothing for seed-level variance, which the proposal itself puts at 1-2 points; a two-sample comparison at n=4/arm with SD=1.5 has an MDE near 3-4 points, worse than the 2-point threshold P2 asks it to resolve, and worse still after the Bonferroni split to alpha=0.025 and the conjunctive rule (pooled CI excludes zero AND all 4 seeds agree in sign AND effect > 2x a between-seed SD estimated from 4 points). The modal outcome is therefore a bounded null on the paper's decisive contrast, on one task with one 7B model. Two secondary defects compound this: (a) the Stage-1 gate selects on the point estimate of D_swap at p=0 being >= 3 points and then folds the gate seed into the pooled analysis, so the headline co-adaptation number is conditioned on having passed a threshold on itself — disclosure does not remove the upward bias; (b) the P8 comparison is asymmetric, taking the best k in {1,2} for p=0 (selected on the same 800 evaluation items, so optimistically biased) against p=0.5 at a fixed k=4 with only a 2-seed spot check at k=2, which means a 'refutation' of P8 could be produced by test-set selection on the competitor alone. Separately, the stated setup 'HotpotQA distractor setting, fullwiki-style tool calls' is internally inconsistent — gold-plus-distractor paragraphs supplied in context is a different task from retrieval tool calls — and HotpotQA contamination in Qwen2.5-7B is a live confound for a study whose banks are distilled from the same dataset.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Five concrete changes, roughly in order of importance. (1) Re-cast the primary endpoint so the degenerate solution cannot win: report memory-conditional gain under turnover, acc(instr, B_B) - acc(instr, no bank), as a co-primary alongside acc under B_swap, and pre-register that a condition with D_swap ~ 0 but zero memory-conditional gain is scored as 'learned to ignore memory', not as robustness. E3 already computes the right quantity (C) but is explicitly non-gating; promote it. (2) Reallocate the envelope from items to seeds: 800 paired items already give a within-seed MDE of 2.5 points, well past the binding constraint, so drop to n=400 items and buy 8-10 optimizer seeds at p=0 and p=0.5. Cutting E5 (8 cells) and E4 entirely funds this; both are explicitly exploratory and neither gates a claim. (3) Move the Stage-1 gate onto a dedicated seed and a dedicated split, and exclude the gate seed from the pooled primary estimate. (4) Make P8 symmetric: tune k per condition over a nested selection split disjoint from the 800 test items, report best-k-for-each rather than best-k-for-the-baseline-only against fixed-k-for-ours. (5) Run and log the dated preprint search now rather than promising it before submission, and add the query terms the current list misses ('prompt optimizer validation overfitting', 'in-context demonstration distribution shift robustness', 'agent memory non-stationarity evaluation', 'DSPy retrieval drift'). Also resolve the HotpotQA distractor-vs-tool-call contradiction and add a contamination check, or move to a task with less exposure.
reviews.missing_baseline: Cross-bank candidate selection. GEPA-style search already produces a pool of candidate instructions and picks one by validation score against the optimization-time bank; the cheapest and most obvious practitioner fix is to keep memory injection on during optimization but select or early-stop the final candidate on a held-out second bank (or on the average over two banks). It costs zero additional rollouts, it is strictly easier to deploy than either memory dropout or shard randomization, and it plausibly captures most of the robustness gain — which would leave the proposal's intervention with no cost advantage over the trivial alternative. Its absence is conspicuous given that the far more expensive 'full re-optimization on every bank change' is included as the upper bound. A second, related omission: joint optimization against both B_A and B_B (multi-bank domain randomization) as the true robustness ceiling, which would bracket shard randomization from above and tell the reader whether p=0.5's gap to the ceiling is 1 point or 6.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check reports that every web-search call failed and that the author has zero verified evidence about recent preprints. By the standard that applies here, that is not a neutral: novelty on both the framing (optimizer-memory co-adaptation as train/deploy context-distribution mismatch) and the diagnostic (bank-swap evaluation of an optimized instruction) is simply unestablished, and this is the second consecutive draft in which the search failed, which reads less like bad luck than like a step that keeps being deferred. The author's mitigation — restructuring the contribution as a comparative fix table so a priority collision is survivable — is the right instinct and is why this is not an automatic reject, but it does not let a reviewer conclude the work is new. I am not able to name a specific colliding arXiv preprint (no search available to me either), so I score this as an unverified novelty claim rather than a demonstrated collision. Two further problems with the check as written: the promised query list omits the terms most likely to surface a collision from the prompt-optimization side rather than the memory side ('prompt optimizer overfits validation context', 'instruction search generalization retrieval shift', 'DSPy/GEPA candidate selection robustness'), and the stated fallback ('if a preprint already performs a bank-swap evaluation, the contribution reduces to the fix table plus P8') understates the damage, since P8's most likely outcome per the proposal's own risk section is that deployment-time top-k tuning wins, leaving a fix table whose headline row is a negative result on the authors' own method.
